results.title: Urban rainfall trends in IMERG datasets
results.text:
2026 · Shankar Sharma, Jason P. Evans, A. J. Pitman · Environmental Research Letters · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study analyzes IMERG satellite data to assess urban rainfall trends in 15 global cities, finding a consistent increase in rainfall frequency and intensity, with microwave-based retrievals dominating the urban signal, and accounting for sampling artefacts reveals a robust and physically consistent urban signal.
Abstract: Abstract Satellite precipitation records are increasingly used to assess whether urbanisation modifies local rainfall. However, it remains unclear whether reported urban signals reflect physical processes or artefacts from evolving satellite observing systems. The Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) merges observations from a growing constellation of microwave and infrared sensors, meaning that long-term trends derived from this product may partly reflect changes in the observing system rather than true precipitation changes. results.title: Evaluation of IMERG climate trends over land in the TRMM and GPM eras
results.text:
2024 · Siyu Zhu, Zhi Li, Mengye Chen · Environmental Research Letters · 8 citations · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study evaluates IMERG's climate trend capturing ability over land from 2001 to 2019, comparing TRMM (2001-2014) and GPM (2015-2019) eras. Results show improved performance in the GPM era, with higher spatial consistency and trend accuracy, suggesting enhanced capacity for tracking global precipitation trends.
Abstract: Abstract The Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission (IMERG) is a global precipitation product suite consisting of both near-real-time and research-grade products with high spatiotemporal resolution. However, the IMERG developers note that it is designed as a High Resolution Precipitation Product (HRPP), not a Climate Data Record (CDR), and its ability to capture climate trends remains uncertain. Therefore, understanding IMERG's capability in capturing climate trends is fundamental. This study examines the climatological performance of IMERG…

results.title: On the Verge of IMERG Version 07
results.text:
2022 · 6 citations · Posted Content
TL;DR: In this article , the authors report the status of IMERG Version 07 processing as of the conference time, and introduce some topics that are being considered for the future, including improved uncertainty estimates, addition of sub-monthly gauge information, and strategies for incorporating precipitation estimates from multiple, relatively short-lived small satellites.
Abstract: Development is well-advanced for the next version of the Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission (IMERG), labeled Version 07. IMERG is a key output of the U.S. GPM Science Team, and V07 will be the second generation in which data from both the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) and GPM projects are combined into a single, uniformly processed record, currently starting in June 2000. This presentation will show several examples of successes and challenges in V06, and use these to illuminate the upgrades that have been pursued for V07.…

TL;DR: In this article , the authors evaluated the dynamic characteristics of the precipitation amounts, intensities, frequencies, and other relevant data across Nepal, using four IMERG datasets: microwave only, infrared only, multi satellites gauge uncalibrated, and multi sensors gauge calibrated.

The integrated multi-satellite retrievals for GPM (IMERG) algorithm combines information from the GPM satellite constellation to estimate precipitation and yields a better performance in detecting precipitation events and spatial resolution. results.title: Impact of Microwave Sounder Calibration on Precipitation for the Global Precipitation Measurement Mission
results.text:
2019 · Rachael Kroodsma · International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium · Proceedings Article
TL;DR: Data is used from past and current microwave sounders to show how offsets in the calibration can impact the precipitation using the GPM Level 2 GPROF algorithm.
Abstract: Cross-track microwave sounders make up a significant percentage of the radiometers included in the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) constellation. Therefore, it is important to properly assess the calibration of each sounder instrument and to understand the impact of the calibration on the derived precipitation rates. This ensures an accurate precipitation product is produced for the entire constellation. results.text:

TL;DR: In this paper , the importance of assessing ensemble flood forecasts with action-relevant scores to support flood preparedness actions by analyzing the discrepancies between traditional general scores that focus on the overall accuracy with other more specific flood event-based scores.
Abstract: This study investigates the importance of assessing ensemble flood forecasts with action-relevant scores to support flood preparedness actions by analyzing the discrepancies between traditional general scores that focus on the overall accuracy with other more specific flood event-based scores. results.title: Enhancing global flood forecasts in Southern Africa using Deep Learning: A user-oriented evaluation for anticipatory actions
results.text:
2025 · Andrea Ficchì, Moslem Mir, Andrea Castelletti · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study evaluates a deep learning model to enhance global flood forecasts in Southern Africa, improving GloFAS predictions up to 7-day lead times, reducing biases, and extending skillful lead times, with added value for anticipatory actions in data-scarce regions.

Humanitarian organizations often integrate these global forecasting systems with local information to assist national mandated agencies in the disaster risk management chain. results.title: Assessing the Riverine Flood Forecast Skill of GloFAS and Google Flood Hub With Impact Data and Discharge Observations to Support Early Actions in Mali
results.text:
2026 · Els Kuipers, Valentijn Oldenburg, Phuoc Phùng · Journal of Flood Risk Management · 1 citations · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study evaluates the flood forecasting skill of GloFAS and Google Flood Hub in Mali, comparing their performance with the current trigger model using discharge observations and impact data, and assessing their potential for anticipatory action in flood-prone regions with limited data availability.
Abstract: ABSTRACT Riverine floods are among the most destructive and frequent natural hazards in Mali. Currently, the protocol relies on upstream water levels from the National Directorate of Hydraulics (DNH) to predict downstream flooding. results.text:

methods_used.evaluation-of-imerg-climate-trends-over-:
- The paper applies the **Mann-Kendall analysis** to evaluate **annual precipitation trends over land** from **2001 to 2019**, using **gauge records as the true values**.  
- It evaluates IMERG **Final (Version 06)** daily precipitation by using **three matching strategies**: matching **at gauge locations**, matching at **0.1° pixels**, and matching at **1.0° pixels**.  
- It performs a **comparative assessment across eras**, separating the record into the **TRMM era (2001–2014)** and the **GPM era (2015–2019)** to examine differences in trend-tracking performance.  
- It uses **reliability/trend-consistency metrics based on agreement with gauge-derived trends**, reporting the **proportion of unreliable samples** and the **proportion of samples showing consistent trends** for each matching strategy and era.
methods_used.evaluation-of-the-spatiotemporal-distrib:
- The study used observational satellite precipitation estimates from four IMERG Final datasets over Nepal for 20 years (2001–2020): microwave only, infrared only, multi-satellites gauge uncalibrated, and multi-satellites gauge calibrated.  
- A set of 28 precipitation indices was computed at IMERG grid locations (and at gauge-station locations for comparison), including threshold-based counts, consecutive wet/dry days, precipitation amounts and extremes, precipitation intensity, percentile-based extremes, proportion-based indices, and additional seasonal spell indices for monsoon dry spells and winter wet spells.  
- The paper handled precipitation data gaps by first filling small gaps using reanalysis or interpolated products via a point-to-pixel approach for gap days: APHRODITE (0.25 spatial resolution) for 2001–2015 and NOAA CPC (0.5 spatial resolution) for 2016–2020; gauge observations were used to generate the gridded products, and the study noted that this filling introduces some uncertainty.  
- Daily IMERG precipitation was used with a 1 mm threshold to define wet and dry days, and the indices were derived from those daily series (for example, wet-day counts, totals over wet days, and intensity based on totals divided by wet-day counts).  
- Trend significance and magnitude were evaluated using a non-parametric Mann–Kendall test with a p-value threshold of 0.1 (90% confidence level), together with the Theil–Sen slope estimator; a pre-whitening method was applied to limit serial correlation using the pyMannKendall workflow.
methods_used.enhancing-global-flood-forecasts-in-sout:
- The paper uses a computational deep-learning approach by developing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)–based post-processing models to improve operational GloFAS river-flow forecasts up to a 7-day lead time.  
- The post-processing models are trained and tested using inputs that include historical GloFAS forecasts of river flows, past forecast errors, and catchment characteristics, with different LSTM architectures and loss functions evaluated to select alternative post-processing variants.  
- The methodology includes both single-site and multi-site modeling strategies, with model performance compared using streamflow observations as a reference in cross-validation.  
- The paper evaluates forecast improvements for operational use by demonstrating changes in skill and value of the forecasts for anticipatory actions, using user-oriented metrics from the Red Cross Early Action Protocol framework for floods in Mozambique (including False Alarm Ratios and Hit Rates).  
- The study uses a valuation framework for early actions to assess the cost-effectiveness of alternative hybrid forecasting solutions for anticipatory actions, and it discusses potential scaling through follow-on post-processing of flood hazard maps.

limitations.evaluation-of-imerg-climate-trends-over-:
- The paper notes that IMERG was designed as a High Resolution Precipitation Product (HRPP), not as a Climate Data Record (CDR), so its ability to capture climate trends remains uncertain.  
- The study evaluates climatological performance using gauge records as the “true values,” implying that conclusions depend on how well gauges represent actual precipitation trends.  
- The analysis is limited to annual precipitation trends over land from 2001 to 2019, split into the TRMM era (2001–2014) and the GPM era (2015–2019), so results may not directly extend to other periods or regions.  
- The comparison shows differences in performance between the TRMM and GPM eras, which the paper attributes to residual differences in calibration methods, indicating a limitation for between-mission consistency.  
- The paper reports different matching strategies (gauge locations, 0.1° pixels, and 1.0° pixels), implying that trend agreement depends on the spatial matching approach used.
limitations.evaluation-of-the-spatiotemporal-distrib:
- The paper reports that most precipitation indices were substantially underestimated, including consecutive wet days, annual and monsoon precipitation, and the days when precipitation equaled or exceeded 20 and 50 mm.  
- It states that the microwave-only dataset highly underestimated precipitation amount.  
- It identifies false alarms as a substantial problem for all four IMERG datasets.  
- It notes that the IMERG uncalibrated dataset tends to overestimate precipitation during heavy precipitation events.  
- It attributes remaining accuracy issues to challenges such as complex topography and atmospheric processes over Nepal, which make precipitation estimation difficult and introduce persistent biases in different regions.
limitations.enhancing-global-flood-forecasts-in-sout:
- The paper states that limitations in the skill of global forecasting systems like GloFAS restrict their operational adoption and constrain the lead times available for implementing early actions.  
- It indicates that, despite the growing number of studies on AI models, there is an urgent need for user-oriented evidence of added value to support operational uptake.  
- It notes that evaluating hybrid forecasting models requires user-oriented criteria (such as False Alarm Ratios and Hit Rates) within a valuation framework of early actions, implying that performance limitations cannot be assessed through standard metrics alone.  
- It suggests that ongoing work is needed on post-processing flood hazard maps to further improve forecast value for early actions.  
- It does not describe additional study-specific limitations in the provided text beyond the above points, so further limitations are not explicitly available from the context.
